<thought>From the 13C NMR spectrum we have ten carbon signals: 166.40, 131.87, 129.70 (two equivalent carbons), 129.01 (two equivalent carbons), 129.00, 52.24, 43.47, and 38.60 ppm. Chemical shifts in the ~110–160 ppm region correspond to aromatic carbons. Counting the signals in that region gives 1 (166.40) + 1 (131.87) + 2 (129.70) + 2 (129.01) + 1 (129.00) = 7 aromatic carbon atoms. The remaining three signals are aliphatic. Therefore the compound contains 7 aromatic carbons.</thought>
<final_answer>7</final_answer>
